title: First blind demand-pull producer goal

goal.description: Oscillator + Envelope + Filter + Macro.Value + proven ModSlot->VoiceFilter modulation route, composed against the bare skeleton, using only currently admitted CapabilityContracts.
goal.note: Not engineered to hit a known weak point -- outcome was not predicted before running.

blockers_encountered.detail: macro_field_value's contract declares prerequisite host:'Filter 1 On', which the caller had not confirmed for this proposed execution context.
blockers_encountered.classification: This was NOT a capability gap. It was 15.4.5's prerequisite-refusal mechanism working exactly as designed -- the caller (this compiler-goal script) simply had not yet supplied proposed_prerequisites_verified.
blockers_encountered.resolution: Re-ran dry_run with proposed_prerequisites_verified={'host:Filter 1 On': True}. No new experiment, no new evidence, no capability promotion was needed.

second_dry_run.context_gaps: none -- ModSlot0 is a plain top-level skeleton key, not a list, so no RequiredContext derivation applied (unlike FXRack0.FX in the earlier FXDistortion.Drive case).

capability_changes.note: No discovery was needed -- the goal succeeded entirely within the frozen 15.5 frontier plus the 16.1-16.3 compiler kernel.

compiler_behavior_observations: The prerequisite-verification refusal correctly fired on the FIRST attempt for a genuinely new reason (never previously exercised in this exact combination) -- proving admission.py's prerequisite check works on a live composition, not just in the adversarial unit tests.

Cross-contract conflict analysis correctly found zero conflicts among 5 real capabilities spanning 4 different top-level modules plus one structured route -- the first time 5 contracts, including a MUTATE_STRUCTURED_VALUE contract, have been composed together.

RequiredContext correctly did NOT fire for ModSlot0, confirming context-gap detection is scoped precisely to list-index descent (FXRack0.FX-shaped paths) and does not over-trigger on ordinary top-level sparse keys.

verification_breakdown.measurement_sensitivity: No recurrence of 16.3-M1's floor-masking pattern observed here -- overall_rms_db detected a clear effect. Not used to close 16.3-M1 (that finding's closure_condition requires a goal specifically testing near-floor vs non-floor witnesses, which this goal did not control for).

open_findings_status.LFO-SOURCE-IDENTITY-1: OPEN, unchanged -- not touched by this goal
open_findings_status.RANDOMPAN-MASKING-1: OPEN, unchanged -- not touched by this goal

derived_next_step: 16.4.1a succeeded without exposing a new gap. Per the demand-pull principle, 16.5 is NOT pre-written from this result -- proceed to 16.4.1b (the LFO->cutoff variant of this same goal, explicitly framed as an attempt to close LFO-SOURCE-IDENTITY-1 via the normal pipeline, not as a fresh discovery) to get the system's first real BLOCKED demand-pull cycle.
